title: Chinchinga Beef Skewers
author: Zoe Adjei
desc: Rump steak in one-centimetre strips with a dry suya mix of cayenne, clove and cinnamon — thirty minutes marinating, three to four minutes a side.
longDesc: The beef version from the same cook who publishes the goat kebabs, and the suya mix here is dry rather than a wet peanut rub: two teaspoons of cayenne, half a teaspoon of smoked paprika, a teaspoon each of ground ginger, nutmeg and garlic powder, half a teaspoon each of cloves and cinnamon, and a teaspoon of crushed sea salt. Five hundred grams of rump steak is cut into one-centimetre strips with fifty grams of grated ginger, marinated at least thirty minutes or up to a day refrigerated, and cooked three to four minutes a side until lightly charred. Her note is that the mix is versatile and can be applied to any meat.
ingredients: 500 g rump steak, cut into 1 cm strips
30 ml groundnut oil, plus extra for brushing
steps: Cut the rump steak into 1 cm strips.
Toss the beef with the grated ginger, cayenne, salt, groundnut oil and the suya mix.
Marinate at least 30 minutes, or up to 1 day refrigerated.
Cook 3 to 4 minutes per side, until lightly charred.
Scatter with the crushed peanuts, sliced red chillies and coriander.
chefTips: Lightly charred is the cue, at three to four minutes a side. Chinchinga wants char marks rather than an even brown.
One-centimetre strips, which is thicker than the quarter-inch of the documented tankora version. Thicker strips suit a shorter, hotter cook.
Fifty grams of grated ginger for five hundred grams of beef is a lot and it tenderises as well as flavours.
Thirty minutes is enough, and up to a day refrigerated is the maximum she gives. Beef does not need overnight the way goat does.
The crushed peanuts go on at the END here, as a garnish, rather than into a rub. That is the opposite of her own goat version, where the peanuts are ground into the marinade.
Cloves and cinnamon in the suya mix are what distinguish this blend. Half a teaspoon each and they are noticeable.
Her own note: the mix is so versatile it can be applied to any meat. Keep a jar of it.
commonMistakes: Strips much thinner than a centimetre, which overcook in three minutes.
Grinding the peanuts into the marinade, which belongs to the goat version.
Cooking to an even brown rather than a light char.
Skipping the ginger, which is doing tenderising work.
sources: TWO PRINTINGS EXIST AND THEY DISAGREE. The version published above is printing (a).

(a) deliciousmagazine.co.uk, 'Chinchinga beef skewers'. BYLINE AS PRINTED: 'By: Zoe Adjonyoh'. Published November 2018, last modified 26 May 2025. Yield as printed: 'Serves: 4'. Equipment as printed: 8-12 skewers. A FETCH CAVEAT: the second fetch WITHHELD the full ingredient list, so THE FULL LIST IS SINGLE-PASS, with only the key quantities repeated on the second pass. Suya mix as printed: 2 tsp cayenne pepper; ½ tsp smoked paprika; 1 tsp each ground ginger, ground nutmeg, garlic powder; ½ tsp each ground cloves, ground cinnamon; 1 tsp crushed sea salt. Main as printed: ½ tsp sea salt; 30ml groundnut oil, plus extra for brushing; 50g fresh ginger, grated; 500g British rump steak, cut into 1cm strips; 1 tsp cayenne pepper; handful fresh coriander; 2-3 red chillies, finely sliced; 100g roasted peanuts, crushed (optional). Method: marinate 'at least 30 minutes (or up to 1 day refrigerated)'; cook '3-4 minutes per side until lightly charred'. Her quote: the mix is 'so versatile and can be applied to any meat'.

(b) vice.com, 'Beef Chichinga Skewers'. BYLINE AS PRINTED: 'By Zoe Adjonyoh'. Dated 25 June 2018, credited to VICE Munchies. 'Servings: 4'. Prep 1 hour, total 1½ hours. AN ATTRIBUTION NOTE: the Vice topic page lists 'How to Improve Your Summer BBQ, Ghanaian Style' as by Ruby Lott-Lavigna, also dated 06.25.18, and whether that is the same piece could not be verified; the recipe page itself reads 'By Zoe Adjonyoh'. Its suya mix as printed on the second fetch: 2 teaspoons ground hot pepper (or cayenne); 1 teaspoon crushed sea salt; 1 teaspoon garlic powder; 1 teaspoon ground ginger; 1 teaspoon ground nutmeg; ½ teaspoon ground cinnamon; ½ teaspoon ground cloves; ½ teaspoon ground ginger; ½ teaspoon smoked paprika. NOTE THAT GINGER APPEARS TWICE WITH DIFFERENT AMOUNTS in that list, and the first fetch listed '2 tsp ground ginger (divided)' instead. THE GINGER QUANTITY IN PRINTING (b) IS UNRESOLVED and is recorded as such. Its skewers, TWO-PASS: '1 pound|500 grams free range rump beef steak'; 2 tablespoons suya spice mix; ½ teaspoon sea salt; '.12 cup|30 ml groundnut oil (20 ml for basting)'; 1 (3-inch) piece ginger, peeled and grated. Method: trim and slice 'approximately 5-inch strips, 1cm wide'; marinate 'minimum 1 hour refrigerated'; 'Grill 3 minutes per side until desired doneness'.

THE DISAGREEMENT, unreconciled: printing (a) has a 30-minute marinade, 50 g of grated ginger, 3-4 minutes per side and 1 cm strips; printing (b) has a 1-hour marinade, a 3-inch ginger piece, 3 minutes per side, strips about 5 inches long and 1 cm wide, and 2 tablespoons of the suya mix measured in. Neither is corrected.

PRINTING (b) ALSO CARRIES A PEANUT SAUCE, SINGLE-PASS: ⅔ cup vegetable stock, 2 cups chalé sauce, 7 oz peanut butter, 'simmer on low for at least 60 minutes', total 2 hours 20 minutes. That is a further printing of the peanut sauce documented at GHA033, whose quantities differ again.

THIS IS THE FOURTH DOCUMENTED CHICHINGA in this collection and the second by this author. The others: beef with a dry tankora coating of de-oiled peanut and toasted corn flour (GHA061); sirloin with a toasted two-blend suya system (GHA062); and kid goat with a WET ground-peanut rub (GHA063). Here the peanuts are a garnish rather than a rub, and the suya mix is dry with cloves and cinnamon. Four named versions, four different approaches.
ON THE SPELLING: chinchinga here, chichinga elsewhere, kyinkyinga in Twi, tsire suya in Nigeria. All the same kebab.
storage: Best at once. 2 days refrigerated cooked.
healthBenefits: Rump steak is high in protein, iron, zinc and vitamin B12.
Roasted peanuts add niacin, vitamin E and monounsaturated fat.
Cloves and cinnamon are among the highest-antioxidant spices measured.
culturalNote: Four published versions of one street kebab, by three cooks, agreeing only that meat goes on a stick with a peanut-and-spice seasoning, is the honest state of chichinga in print. This one is the easiest to make on a weeknight and the suya mix keeps, which is probably why it exists in two outlets.
